# ax-claims

The Ouro AX standard as data: a claim is one checkable rule about an interface an agent uses, with the reason, the evidence that admitted it, the check `ax-xray` runs and the fix. A claim is `must` only when an evaluation showed agents failing without it, or when it guards against a stated safety, compatibility or integrity hazard; every other claim is `should`.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ax-claims#v1.3.0
```

It installs `lib/ouro/ax/claims.ts`. Its tests are `ax-claims-tests`. Every item runs on Node 22.18 or later as it is copied: the files import each other as `./<file>.ts`. The [Ouro AX guide](../guides/ax.md) shows how they fit together.

## Exports

### `checkClaimSet`

The problems with a claim set, one line each with the fix: a missing field, a repeated id, an unknown surface, tier or scope, and a `must` claim the admission rule does not allow (one that rests on a principle, an evaluation without its run, or a hazard not stated).

```ts
function checkClaimSet(value: unknown): string[]
```

### `Claim`

```ts
interface Claim {
  id: string;
  surface: ClaimSurface;
  tier: ClaimTier;
  applies: ClaimScope;
  rule: string;
  why: string;
  evidence: ClaimEvidence;
  check: string;
  fix: string;
}
```

### `CLAIM_SCOPES`

```sh
Which surfaces a claim applies to. The X-ray decides it from what the interface says about itself (`help --json`, the
routes manifest, tools/list), not from a hand-written waiver:
- `interface`: once per interface.
- `command`, `read`, `others`, `text`, `wait`: CLI commands, the reads among them (effect private), those other people
see, those that take free text, and the wait command.
- `events`: the work-event read the adopter names.
- `route`, `read-route`, `ref-route`, `others-route`: HTTP routes that answer an error, GET routes, routes with an id
in the path, and the probes of writes other people see.
- `tool`, `tool-required`: MCP tools, and those with required arguments.
```

```ts
const CLAIM_SCOPES: readonly ["interface", "command", "read", "others", "text", "wait", "events", "route", "read-route", "ref-route", "others-route", "tool", "tool-required"]
```

### `CLAIM_SET`

The claims of this version of Ouro AX. Evidence paths are relative to the Ouro UI repository (https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui).

```ts
const CLAIM_SET: ClaimSet
```

### `CLAIM_SET_VERSION`

The Ouro AX standard as data: a claim is one checkable rule about an interface an agent uses, with the reason, the evidence that admitted it, the check `ax-xray` runs and the fix. A claim is `must` only when an evaluation showed agents failing without it, or when it guards against a stated safety, compatibility or integrity hazard; every other claim is `should`.

```ts
const CLAIM_SET_VERSION: "1.1.0"
```

### `ClaimEvidence`

Why a claim is in the standard. `evaluation`: an agent evaluation (`source` is the run's file); `hazard`: the harm it guards against, in `finding`; `principle`: a design principle, not yet shown by a run (`should` only).

```ts
interface ClaimEvidence {
  basis: "evaluation" | "hazard" | "principle";
  source: string;
  finding: string;
}
```

### `ClaimScope`

```ts
type ClaimScope = (typeof CLAIM_SCOPES)[number];
```

### `ClaimSet`

```ts
interface ClaimSet {
  version: string;
  claims: readonly Claim[];
}
```

### `claimSetText`

The claim set as canonical JSON (keys sorted), the text its hash is taken over.

```ts
function claimSetText(set: ClaimSet): string
```

### `ClaimSurface`

```ts
type ClaimSurface = "cli" | "http" | "mcp";
```

### `ClaimTier`

```ts
type ClaimTier = "must" | "should";
```

### `loadClaimSet`

A claim set read from JSON (an adopter's own copy, say), checked; throws with every problem when it is not one.

```ts
function loadClaimSet(value: unknown): ClaimSet
```
